bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — (c) IS DUE TODAY AND IS STILL UNRUN AT THE SECOND FIRE; (a) DUE TOMORROW; (b) AND (e) DUE SEP 12
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions, carried forward from the 06:04 fire so nothing this morning found is lost. (a) misalignment / MCP incident log - DUE TOMORROW SEP 11, and it is no longer a design problem: Anthropic's Compliance API now returns consolidated Cowork and Claude Code session transcripts including MCP tool-call content with per-message IDs and timestamps, which is the corrected specification, so (a) is a build-or-buy decision (Enterprise tier, or hand-roll the same five-field record). (b) Entra's four MCP controls as a config script - DUE SEP 12. (c) /skill-doctor across the ~130-skill corpus - DUE TODAY, runnable since Sep 4 in v2.1.261, with one real gate: it is a Claude Code terminal command while the corpus loads into Cowork. (e) cadence-cost measurement before the Sep 14 Claude Code limit change - DUE SEP 12, and bullet 2 changes its arithmetic. Also standing from 06:04 and unactioned: the built-in browser split (credentialed work stays in the attached Chrome, measurement work moves to the isolated built-in profile) - a one-line amendment to three skills.
bullets.how: YES. The only new fact this fire can add to the list is the clock: (c) was due at 00:00 today, the second fire of the day is now writing about it, and no number from /skill-doctor exists. Note what bullet 2 does to the standing list - it supplies a MECHANICAL cause for the week's three misses (Cognition, HiddenLayer, /skill-doctor) that no amount of rule-writing would have found, and it is a settings problem rather than a discipline problem. That is the first item this week that is cheaper to fix than to diagnose.

bullets.title: THE DAY'S LEAD - ANTHROPIC'S OWN DOCS NAME THE MECHANISM BEHIND THIS REPORT'S THREE MISSES: FABLE 5.1 'ANSWERS FROM MEMORY MORE OFTEN AT LOW EFFORT', CALLING SEARCH LESS - AND CACHE READS NOW COST A QUARTER, WHICH RE-PRICES ACTION (e)
bullets.summary: The Fable 5.1 behaviour-differences page lists changes that appear with no code change. Three are load-bearing for us. (1) 'Answers from memory more often at low effort' - at the lowest effort level the model calls a search or retrieval tool LESS often; the documented fixes are to raise effort for turns needing fresh information, including mid-conversation, or add an explicit verification nudge. (2) Cache reads are $0.25/MTok, 0.025x base input rather than the usual 0.1x, so long agentic sessions that re-read a cached prefix pay a quarter of the Fable 5 rate. (3) Effort defaults differ by surface - Fable 5.1 defaults to HIGH effort in Claude Code and MEDIUM in Cowork and on claude.ai - and per-message effort is now changeable mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache (beta header mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01). Also documented: more variable parallel tool calling (one call per turn where Fable 5 batched several), fewer progress updates at higher effort, and a tendency to rewrite whole files for small edits.
bullets.how: YES, and this is the most useful thing this report has found about ITSELF. Yesterday's praxis lesson concluded 'we check what is newest and never check what is true' and prescribed discipline. Anthropic documents a mechanism instead: at low effort the model ANSWERS FROM MEMORY RATHER THAN SEARCHING. A daily scan is precisely a task whose correctness depends on retrieval firing every time, and Cowork - where this scan runs - defaults to MEDIUM, not the HIGH that Claude Code gets. So the concrete fix for (a)-through-(e)'s recurring staleness is a settings change plus one prompt line, not a seventh rule: raise effort on scan turns, or carry an explicit verification nudge in the task file. Second: this materially changes standing action (e). The Sep 14 limit change was being modelled against Fable 5 economics, and a 4x cheaper cache read means our long agentic sessions - render loops, the answer-page factory, this scan - are cheaper per re-read than the (e) worksheet assumes; measuring cadence cost on Sep 12 against stale prices would produce a wrong number. Third, two operational collisions worth naming now: whole-file rewrites for small edits runs against one-canonical-file and inflates diffs on B9 page work, and less parallel tool calling means our throughput skills should carry the documented one-line batching instruction.

bullets.title: EVERY IMAGE, VIDEO AND AUDIO FILE CLAUDE PRODUCES NOW CARRIES SIGNED C2PA CONTENT CREDENTIALS, AND ALL FABLE 5.1 TEXT CARRIES A STATISTICAL WATERMARK
bullets.summary: Content provenance shipped with Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. Text generated by these models carries Anthropic's statistical text watermark on every platform where the model is available - it adds no tokens or hidden characters, carries no information about the user or organisation, and does not change meaning or readability. Supported image, video and audio files Claude produces, for example through the code execution tool, carry signed C2PA Content Credentials when retrieved through the Files API on the Claude API.
bullets.how: YES, and it lands directly on the client-facing side of the business rather than the tooling side. Two consequences. For VironBox / STRUCTA: our standing rule is ZERO generative AI on the building, and provenance metadata now makes that rule AUDITABLE rather than merely asserted - a render that came out of Blender/Cycles on our own geometry carries no Content Credential, and anything that passed through a model does. That is a defensible claim to a developer client and it costs nothing to adopt, but it also means any AI-touched asset we ship is now self-identifying to anyone who inspects it, so the ai-render-full-frame-review gate should add a provenance check before send. For Brand 9 and Nana Buns: images generated through Claude's file path now carry credentials into whatever we publish, which is fine where we say so and awkward where a page implies photography. Scope it honestly - this covers files retrieved via the Files API on the Claude API, and our Higgsfield-through-the-browser path is a separate pipeline this does not describe. The action is one line in the render-review gate and one line in b9-claims-truth-gate, not a policy rewrite.

bullets.title: THE MCP MAINTAINERS HAVE MADE OUR ~130-SKILL CONTEXT TAX A PROTOCOL PRIORITY - 'PROGRESSIVE DISCOVERY' - AND AGENT IDENTITY IS THE UPSTREAM OF STANDING ACTION (b)
bullets.summary: The new MCP roadmap sets five priority areas: agentic messaging primitives, HTTP-native transport unification, agent identity and enterprise-ready security, improved primitives, and SDK developer experience. Under improved primitives the maintainers state the scale problem plainly - connecting to a server with a hundred tools means the model pays for that entire surface before the user has asked a single question, and tool selection gets worse as the list grows - and are starting a progressive-discovery effort so a server can offer a small entry point and reveal more of its catalogue as the conversation narrows. Under agent identity they are finalising DPoP (RFC 9449) and defining a path through Workload Identity Federation and the ID-JAG grant behind Enterprise-Managed Authorization, which is now stable, because today's authorization assumes a person approving access in a browser rather than an agent running as a cloud workload. Source-quality note: this roadmap was published Aug 22, not in the last 24h; it is carried because bullet 2 and standing action (c) are the same problem stated from the other end. SEPs outside the five areas get deprioritised review.
bullets.how: YES, and the value is that it settles an argument (c) keeps having with itself. 'A hundred tools charged before the first question' is our ~130-skill corpus described by the people who own the protocol, which means the economy tax is STRUCTURAL, not a sign we over-collected skills - so (c)'s output should be an economy NUMBER and a load-order, not a guilt-driven prune list. Progressive discovery is the same shape as our own skill descriptions doing trigger-matching before a skill body loads, so the architecture we already run is the direction the protocol is heading; that is a reason to keep the corpus and instrument it. On (b): Entra's four controls are the vendor expression of the agent-identity area, and DPoP plus workload identity is where pasted API keys and long-lived tokens go to die - relevant because our credential routing still leans on stored keys. Do not overstate it - a roadmap is intent, not shipped capability, and none of this is actionable code this week.

bullets.title: SOMEONE JUST RAISED $5M TO TURN CONSTRUCTION DRAWINGS INTO TRACEABLE SCOPES OF WORK - THE EXACT SHAPE OF THE B9 TAKEOFF AND THE VIRONBOX PROVENANCE GATE
bullets.summary: Wyre AI emerged from stealth on Sep 10 with $5M in pre-seed and seed funding, the seed led by Ironspring Ventures with WND Ventures (DPR Construction's corporate venture arm) and the Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation participating. Founded by Pype founder Sunil Dorairajan, the preconstruction platform reads a full document set and produces two things: Wyre Scopes, which identifies every scope of work and delivers scope packages with TRACEABLE REFERENCES BACK TO THE SOURCE DOCUMENTS for preconstruction teams to refine, and Wyre Check, which flags clashes between the documents and the resulting shop drawings. Corroborated across ENR, Dealroom and the Sep 10 funding roundup; the $5M and the investor list are company-reported at announcement.
bullets.how: MAYBE - not a tool to adopt, but the closest adjacency this report has surfaced to what B9 and VironBox actually do. Brand 9 reads builder plan sets and turns them into sign scopes and takeoffs by hand; Wyre is that motion, funded, for the general-contractor side. Two readings. The threat reading is thin: preconstruction scope packages for GCs are not signage takeoff, the founder's distribution comes from Pype and DPR, and nothing suggests a move toward trade-specific packages. The useful reading is the product shape - TRACEABLE REFERENCES BACK TO THE SOURCE DOCUMENT is exactly our vironbox-provenance-gate discipline, sold as the headline feature, which is confirmation that in construction the citation IS the product and not a compliance chore. If a B9 takeoff or an ANS scope ever ships as a client deliverable, it should carry the same per-line source reference, because that is what the market is being taught to expect. Filed maybe: it changes no build this week, and the honest use is as a design reference plus one name on Scout's construction-adjacent watch list.

praxis_lesson: For six fires this report has explained its own staleness with rules - external clocks, boundary-is-not-coverage, memory, and yesterday's 'we check what is newest and never check what is true.' Today Anthropic's own model documentation supplies a MECHANISM that no rule would have found: Fable 5.1 ANSWERS FROM MEMORY MORE OFTEN AT LOW EFFORT, calling search and retrieval tools less, and Cowork - where this scan runs - defaults to MEDIUM effort while Claude Code defaults to HIGH. A daily research scan is the single task type whose correctness depends entirely on retrieval firing, and it has been running on the surface with the lower default. That does not excuse the three misses - Cognition, HiddenLayer, /skill-doctor - but it reframes them: we were writing discipline for a configuration problem. THE LESSON IS THAT WHEN A FAILURE REPEATS ACROSS DIFFERENT MECHANISMS AND DIFFERENT DAYS, THE NEXT MOVE IS TO READ THE SETTINGS AND THE VENDOR'S BEHAVIOUR NOTES, NOT TO WRITE A SEVENTH RULE. The corollary is uncomfortable and worth stating: five of this week's fires produced correct diagnoses of a problem that a documentation page had already explained. Concretely, three things are now cheap and none require more scanning - raise effort or carry a verification nudge on scan turns; re-price (e)'s Sep 12 cadence measurement against the new 0.025x cache-read rate before the Sep 14 limit change, because the old worksheet is wrong; and run (c), which was due at midnight and is still unrun at the second fire of the day.
